indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other
something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the letters of hacienda are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish abandoned in a dilapidated Mexican ranch house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns HACIENDA into ENCHIADA, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican dish of a rolled tortilla with a savoury filling, so it is an example of food.

indicators.note: wayward means straying from the proper course, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about some people's unruly attitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' rearranges THOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The characteristic spirit and beliefs of a group or person, its outlook and attitudes.

clue.text: Section without deliveries is on the slide

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a clip is a short section cut from a film
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by the bowler, so deliveries gives overs

explanation.surface: A cricket team's fielding section with no bowling to face is sliding downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket vocabulary misleads: 'without' here means outside, not lacking, and 'is' is a link word. An over is six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin glass square laid over a specimen sits on top of a microscope slide, so it is described as on the slide.

clue.text: In a short time a prisoner becomes disloyal

indicators.note: In placed first tells us that the next piece goes inside another

parts.note: an instant is a very short time
con is short for convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: Someone who quickly turns traitor after being jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like the start of a phrase but is the container signal; 'becomes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inconstant is changeable and unfaithful, which is a synonym of disloyal.

parts.note: an ass is a stupid person, a blockhead
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
Dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D

explanation.surface: An undeniable fool gazing down on a Scottish or Welsh river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Dee' looks like the real river but splits into a river and a spelt-out letter; 'overlooking' puts the blockhead on top in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Assured means guaranteed or certain, so it can describe something beyond refutation.

clue.text: Al names Dickey in sign language

indicators.note: dickey is slang for shaky or unsound, so the letters of Al names are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man called Al names a Dickensian fellow in sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickey', a British word meaning faulty or unsound, rearranges AL NAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ameslan is an abbreviation of American Sign Language, so it is a particular sign language.

clue.text: Raise one gets in the army

indicators.note: the piece for one gets in, entering the other piece

parts.note: a host is an archaic word for an army
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A recruit lifted up as soon as he enlists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' puts I inside HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to lift or raise it, often with ropes.

indicators.note: conceals means one piece hides the other inside itself

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor

explanation.surface: A bad actor hides an uncommon wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' puts R inside HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm means damage or hurt, a synonym of injury.

indicators.note: a hotel flying a flag has the flag above it, so in this down clue the flag piece sits on top

parts.note: the yellow flag is a species of iris
Hotel is H in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Irish hotel has a flag flying over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' suggests a banner but is the iris plant; 'flies' puts IRIS on top of H in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian means of Ireland.

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters of thy career are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone accused of disloyalty that ruined another's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges THY CAREER.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is the breaking of trust, a synonym of betrayal.

clue.text: Ruin part of "Man of la Mancha" vocal score

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters lying inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A section of the musical's score spoils everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' points to the letters running across the end of Mancha and the start of vocal; 'score' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread destruction, so it is a noun synonym of ruin.

clue.text: Subordinate holds fruit for the men of the family

indicators.note: holds means one piece contains the other

parts.note: side as an adjective means subordinate or secondary, as in a side issue
pears are fruit

explanation.surface: A junior servant keeps fruit set aside for the menfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' is the container signal; 'for' is a link word. The spear side contrasts with the distaff (female) side.
explanation.definitionFit: The spear side is an old term for the male line of descent in a family, as opposed to the distaff side.

parts.note: a spring is a natural source of water, like a well
to roll out is to spread something flat, as with pastry or a carpet

explanation.surface: A Chinese meal that is nicely laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well spread' reads as praise for a buffet, but the two words are taken separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A pancake rolled round a filling and fried, a dish of Chinese cooking.

clue.text: Elegant young woman rudely cut short

indicators.note: cut short means losing the last letter, done abruptly here

parts.note: chick is a slang word for a young woman

explanation.surface: A stylish girl is brusquely interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely cut short' removes the K from CHICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, a synonym of elegant.

clue.text: Union supporter trips in British Museum — help needed

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rides are trips or journeys
aid means help

explanation.surface: A trade unionist stumbles in a London museum and needs assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' is a marriage, not a trade union; 'in' is the container signal and 'needed' a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attends the bride at a wedding, the union of a couple, so she supports it.

clue.text: Acted without past being enlarged upon

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: did means acted or performed
late means past, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Someone behaved with no history, as if exaggerated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking; 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate upon a subject is to speak or write about it at length, to expand on it.

indicators.note: eating means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: deer are animals
liver is a kind of offal

explanation.surface: A rescuer of creatures that feed on innards.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliverer is one who sets people free, a rescuer or saviour.

indicators.note: the original form of the word Turner is taken on a tour, turning its letters about

parts.note: U is the British label for upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: The painter J. M. W. Turner first travelled round an exclusive school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a verb here; 'originally toured' rearranges TURNER with U.
explanation.definitionFit: To school a child is to train and bring them up, a synonym of nurturing them.

clue.text: A French woman has a couple of articles to uncover

parts.note: un is French for a
she refers to a woman
the indefinite article and the definite article in English
the second of the two English articles

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman owns a couple of items she wants to reveal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe a sword is to draw it out of its scabbard, so to uncover it.

clue.text: Long to interrupt stars in battle scene

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: Leo is a constellation of stars
to pant for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A yearning breaks in on the heavens above a place of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to interrupt' is the container signal and 'in' a link word; Leo is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepanto, off Greece, was the scene of a famous naval battle in 1571.

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so the letters of Salerno are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fabric made in an Italian port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges SALERNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Orleans is a fabric of cotton warp and worsted weft, a kind of cloth.

parts.note: a mode is a method or approach
a sty is a filthy dwelling, a hovel

explanation.surface: A humble way of drawing near a shack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is a lack of vanity about oneself, a synonym of humility.

indicators.note: concealing means one piece hides the other inside it

parts.note: to mate is to couple or pair
Che Guevara is the famous guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: A pair of people hiding a rebel's blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guerrilla's' points to Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife that can be used as a weapon.

indicators.note: covers means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to vet something is to examine or survey it

explanation.surface: An inspection of tiny undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' puts VET round S.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest is a British undergarment worn on the upper body.

parts.note: to sap is to drain someone's strength
the ide or id is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Emptying out a fish that tastes good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means having a strong pleasant taste, so it is close to delicious.

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as unions did
Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk in David Copperfield by Charles Dickens

explanation.surface: A scoundrel shuns a sly clerk from a Victorian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is an oily clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: The black sheep of a family is the disreputable member, the ne'er-do-well.

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
IL is the international code for Israel

explanation.surface: A menace posed by a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: IL is the two-letter country code for Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious danger, a synonym of threat.

clue.text: Old bird sitting on pole is grouse

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: the moa is an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: An ancient bird perched on a post is a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' suggests the game bird, but it is the verb or noun meaning complain.
explanation.definitionFit: A moan is a complaint, as is a grouse in its slang sense.

indicators.note: cuts means one piece slices into the other

parts.note: a rebate is money paid back
pro is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A brazen sex worker trims a refund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shameless' is used as the noun-like adjective; 'cuts' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is unprincipled and without shame, so the adjective means shameless.

indicators.note: empty-headed here means losing the head, the first letter

parts.note: a factor is a Scottish land agent or steward

explanation.surface: A foolish estate manager is childish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'juvenile' is a noun: a performer who plays youthful roles; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre a juvenile is a performer who plays young parts, so a type of performer.

clue.text: Hazardous gas produces confusion among sailors

indicators.note: among means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, sailors
ado is fuss and confusion

explanation.surface: A dangerous gas causes chaos aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is the container signal; 'produces' is a link word. RN, the Royal Navy, is a stock crossword source for sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, dangerous when it builds up in homes.

parts.note: to career is to rush along at speed
well can mean profitably or advantageously, as in doing well

explanation.surface: A woman named Veronica has a lucrative career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronica' looks like a woman's name but is the plant genus; 'makes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the botanical genus name for the speedwell flowers.
